summary: Obfuscated WordPress account-takeover payload distributed via npm
details: The package's single main file is a heavily obfuscated browser IIFE (unicode-escape identifiers, reversed string literals, XOR-noise variables) that runs at module top level and targets the WordPress site noviembrenacional.com. It gates on window.location.href containing 'noviembrenacional.com', reads document.documentElement.outerHTML and POSTs the base64-encoded page to a hardcoded canarytokens.com submit endpoint (http://canarytokens.com/articles/tags/images/j11lq4swuzvslc96qfi9pmsji/submit.aspx), then, if the currently logged-in WordPress user is not 'JuanCuesta', fetches /my-account/edit-account/, scrapes the WordPress save-account-details nonce, and POSTs a form that rewrites the victim's account_email to the hardcoded attacker address nyxalor_25@proton.me — an account-takeover primitive that lets the attacker trigger a password reset. The package has no library API, no benign functionality, and its declared purpose does not match its contents. It is a weaponized cross-site payload published as an npm module.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
